topic.title: UPI never felt like it cost anything
topic.claim: We stopped thinking of UPI as money leaving and started treating it as a reflex, and a 0.4% charge is the first time the reflex has a price tag in the room.
topic.behaviour: Scanning a QR for everything, from the big electronics bill to the small one, without ever thinking about who pays for the rail underneath.
topic.mechanism: Zero visible friction makes spending feel weightless. When a merchant has to pay on a ₹2,000-plus payment, the invisible cost can turn into a surcharge or a 'cash de do' at the counter, and we notice only then.
real_details: From 15 October a 0.4% merchant charge applies to person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000
Railways, telecom, fuel and insurance pay a flat ₹5 instead
Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month via QR are exempt
The government says consumers pay nothing directly and about 96% of merchant transactions are unaffected
Average daily UPI volume reached 802 million in September, a first
The Supreme Court declined to stay the rule and asked the Centre to justify the ₹2,000 threshold
topic.news_peg: 0.4% UPI merchant charge above ₹2,000 effective 15 October 2026, after UPI's record daily volume in September 2026
topic.why_now: The rule just took effect, and the first surcharge or cash request at a shop is likely to be this month.

score.why: Names the exact UPI merchant fee and turns a daily reflex into a priced moment, same move as the QR-sticker and GST 2.0 takes he kept.

topic.title: The bank we never leave
topic.claim: We will switch phones, apps and jobs, but the salary account stays where HR opened it, and banks know it.
topic.behaviour: Sitting with one bank for years, grumbling about each new charge, and still never moving.
topic.mechanism: Inertia and paperwork dread. The account feels like a household appliance, not a product you shop for. That loyalty is what lets small fees creep in quietly.
real_details: From 1 October SBI salary-package holders get 5 free other-bank ATM transactions a month, down from 10
After that, a cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST
Basic savings accounts pay ₹15 plus GST per withdrawal beyond four a month
From 1 October RBI rules require the same rate on similar deposits accepted the same day at any branch and published rate schedules
Salaried users are complaining about creeping bank charges
topic.news_peg: SBI ATM limit cut and RBI deposit-rate rules, both from 1 October 2026
topic.why_now: Both changes landed together this month and show how much banks rely on us staying put.

score.why: Concrete, plain reframe on how banks profit off our inertia, no company blamed for wrongdoing, just the pattern, like the bestseller-tag take.

topic.title: A 'no' in arranged marriage costs different people differently
topic.claim: In the arranged-marriage market, saying no is free for one side, and the other side can pay for it with her reputation.
topic.behaviour: A poster describes a friend who rejects matches by telling the girls' fathers made-up things, such as that the daughter has a boyfriend, and who is backed by the friend circle. The poster is shocked and wants out of the group.
topic.mechanism: Rejection happens between families through phone calls, without an appeal or a witness. When a past hurt meets that setup, a bitter person can turn it into a quiet weapon, and the group's silence tells him it's fine. The system relies on word of mouth and gives the woman's side little way to answer.
topic.group: young adults in the arranged-marriage market and their friend circles
real_details: A 28-year-old man is meeting girls through arranged marriage
He rejects them by saying fake things about the matches
He told one father that his daughter had a boyfriend and wasn't serious about AM
He has recently rejected two girls this way
The poster says the friend circle supported his decision
The poster doesn't want to stay in the friend group
topic.why_now: The wedding and matchmaking season is picking up, and the post got strong traction on the subreddit.

score.why: Pushes the matrimony-filter insight one notch further: saying no is free for one side and costs the other her name, the kind of asymmetry he likes to name.

topic.title: Fandom is unpaid marketing and we love it
topic.claim: Opening day of Jailer 2 and half a million shares of a Prabhas poster show that fans don't just watch the film, they run its campaign for free and feel proud doing it.
topic.behaviour: Booking the first show, sharing posters and teasers, tracking records in the group chat, and celebrating a hero's birthday as a holiday.
topic.mechanism: Belonging. Sharing a poster is a public vote for 'my side', and a record broken by the film feels like a personal win.
real_details: Jailer 2 released on 15 October with ₹125.25 crore worldwide gross on Day 1 per The Week, ₹127.25 crore per Sacnilk
About ₹209 crore in two days by Sacnilk's early estimate, and India net fell about 40% from Day 1
It is the fourth Tamil film of 2026 to cross ₹200 crore worldwide
The Karnataka and Kerala Tamil-film records are being widely shared by fans
Prabhas's Fauzi first-look poster drew more than 544,000 Instagram shares in 24 hours, according to the makers
The Fauzi teaser is set for his birthday, 23 October, and the release shift to 18 March 2027 is unconfirmed
topic.news_peg: Jailer 2 opening and Fauzi teaser build-up, October 2026
topic.why_now: A huge Tamil opening and a big teaser date fall in the same week.

score.why: Flips his influencer-marketing belief: fans run the film's PR for free and feel proud doing it, fresh angle on a belief he already argues from.
